title: A group has turned on you at work or online
lede: It is not one person any more. There is a group — a team, a chat, a comment section — and the story has hardened into a version of you that you do not recognise. New people keep arriving already convinced.

blocks.text: It is not one person any more. There is a group — a team, a chat, a comment section — and the story has hardened into a version of you that you do not recognise. New people keep arriving already convinced.

items: A pile-on is not a debate and it cannot be won by argument. Each reply is fuel and extends the lifespan of the event.
Most participants have almost no stake. They will lose interest within days unless you keep supplying material.
The small number who actually matter — your manager, your client, your family, the decider — need one clear message. Everyone else needs nothing.
Your instinct to defend yourself everywhere is the mechanism by which these events grow.

items.detail: Not a dignified last word, not one clarification. Silence starves it in a way nothing else does.

items.move: Preserve evidence before it is deleted
items.detail: Screenshots with dates, URLs, names. Take them now — the worst material disappears first.

items.move: Write one short factual statement, and only where it is needed
items.detail: To your manager, your client, your family. Three sentences: what happened, what did not, what you are doing.

items.move: Separate the true part from the false part
items.detail: If there is a genuine fault in there, own it once, precisely and without theatre. Partial ownership ends far more of these than total denial.

items.move: Get off the platform for 48 hours
items.detail: Delegate monitoring to one friend. Reading it hourly damages your judgement exactly when you need it.

items.move: Tell your employer before they hear it elsewhere
items.detail: A short, calm heads-up from you beats a forwarded screenshot from a stranger.

items.say: "You may see something about me circulating. Here is what actually happened, here is what is inaccurate, and I am not responding to it publicly."
"I got the second part wrong and I have corrected it. The rest of what is being said is not accurate."
"I am not doing a running commentary on it. I am fine. Ask me in a fortnight."
"This has a shelf life. My job is to not extend it."

items: The long explanatory post or thread. It becomes the new artefact and is quoted for years.
Deleting your entire history in a panic. It reads as guilt and destroys your own evidence.
Rallying your own counter-mob. It doubles the event and makes you a combatant rather than a target.
Legal threats fired off in anger. They are screenshotted and they escalate everything.
Making irreversible life decisions during the first week.
Check the search results for your name in a month and address only what is still live.
Repair privately with individuals who matter, one at a time. That is where reputation actually rebuilds.
Expect the delayed emotional bill roughly a fortnight later, when it has gone quiet and you finally stop running on adrenaline.
If it was work-related, get the outcome documented so it cannot be revived vaguely later.

limit: If it includes threats of violence, your home address, sexual content, or targeting of your children, it has crossed into criminal harassment in most jurisdictions. Report it with your evidence, get a reference number, and stop handling it as a reputation problem.
